name: TWO WORLDS, ONE FRAME
message:
Take a picture and transform it into a seamless split-frame digital collage in the tradition of contemporary contrast-collage artists who juxtapose two starkly different realities within a single continuous photograph. The subject occupies one half of the frame, fully integrated into an IDYLLIC WORLD scene. The other half of the SAME continuous frame — sharing consistent lighting logic, horizon lines, and perspective so it reads as one impossible photograph, not two pasted together — depicts THE OTHER SIDE, a starkly harder reality. The two halves meet at a deliberate visual SEAM that makes the collision unmistakable rather than hidden.

SELECTION LOGIC (CRITICAL):
• The options list below contains three categories of ten, in this fixed order: IDYLLIC WORLD (options 001-010), THE OTHER SIDE (options 011-020), THE SEAM (options 021-030)
• If no master prompt specifies otherwise, select exactly ONE option from EACH of the three categories — never three from the same category
• If randomizeOptions is used, randomize the selection independently within each category, not across the full list

CRITICAL:
• The seam must be a clear formal device — this is a collage confronting the viewer with contrast, not a seamless blend that hides the split
• Color grading should shift meaningfully across the seam — warmer/more saturated on the idyllic side, cooler/more desaturated on the other
• The subject should appear ONLY on the idyllic side, fully present and photorealistic; the other side should read as environment and circumstance, not as a depiction of the subject or any other identifiable person in distress
• This format is meant to provoke reflection on inequality and contrast, not to shock or sensationalize

additionalInstructions: HARD CONSTRAINTS: Do not depict graphic violence, injury, death, or bodies of any kind. Do not depict any real, specific, named current or historical conflict, disaster, or country/region intended to be recognized as a real event. Do not depict any real, identifiable public figure. Do not depict the subject, or any other person, appearing distressed, injured, or in danger on 'the other side' — that side should be told through environment and circumstance, never through a person's suffering. The goal is to provoke reflection on inequality and contrast, evoking empathy through juxtaposition rather than shock through explicit suffering.
